title: Three-axis Active Magnetic Compensation with Spatial Feedforward Matrix Decoupling and Hysteresis PI Regulation for Suppressing Zeeman Decoherence of Cold Atom Quantum Memories
authors: Ya Li, Xiao-Long Zou, Xiang-Yao Liang, Chang-Qing Niu, Xin Guo, Wei-Zhe Qiao, You-Xing Chen
abstract: Cold-atom quantum memories require a near-zero magnetic environment (residual field <1 microtesla) to mitigate Zeeman decoherence. Conventional three-axis active compensation suffers from inter-coil crosstalk and geomagnetic drift, which degrade the uniformity and long-term stability of the zero-field region. To address this, we propose a spatiotemporally cooperative feedback-controlled suppression architecture for magnetic interference. An integrally printed three-dimensional orthogonal coil frame mechanically suppresses inter-axis flux leakage. A spatial feedforward inverse matrix is introduced to algorithmically eliminate first-order cross-coupling. A dual-threshold hysteresis incremental-PI controller filters magnetometer quantization fluctuations and avoids frequent small jitter adjustments of coil driving currents. Hardware ablation experiments, long-duration stability tests and spatial magnetic-field mapping were conducted. Experimental results show that during a 714.4 s continuous steady-hold stage, the mean and maximum residual fields at the central point reach 0.112 microtesla and 0.224 microtesla, respectively. The overlapping Allan deviations of all three components remain below 5 nT for averaging times of 1.9-178.2 s. Based on differential-ferrofluid lattice-scan measurements combined with centre-constrained quadratic vector reconstruction and soft Maxwell regularization, a weak-field spatial distribution with an RMS variation of 5.65 microtesla is fitted within a spherical region of interest of radius 5 mm, where 67.5% of the model volume meets the sub-5 microtesla coverage criterion. For a prolate ellipsoidal region matching the atomic-cloud distribution with full axis lengths of 10, 5, and 5 mm, the upper field bound within 93.7% of the volume is 2.68 microtesla.
summary: This paper presents an advanced, integrated hardware and software solution to actively compensate for magnetic field inhomogeneities that cause decoherence in cold atom quantum memories. By combining a specialized coil geometry, feedforward decoupling, and a hysteresis-controlled PI loop, the system achieves unprecedented temporal and spatial stability in the near-zero magnetic field regime. This work is crucial for realizing robust, long-lived quantum memory platforms.
main_problem: The primary challenge is suppressing Zeeman decoherence in cold atom quantum memories, which necessitates maintaining an extremely uniform and near-zero residual magnetic field.
main_result: The proposed integrated system achieved exceptional stability, reaching mean residual fields of $0.112 \mu	ext{T}$ over long hold times and demonstrating high spatial uniformity, with $93.7\%$ of the target volume meeting the sub-$5 \mu	ext{T}$ criterion.
method: The authors developed a spatiotemporally cooperative feedback control architecture combining mechanical coil design, algorithmic feedforward decoupling, and a dual-threshold hysteresis PI controller.
model_or_system: The system uses a triaxial active magnetic compensation platform with an orthogonal coil frame to stabilize the magnetic environment for cold atoms. The control loop compensates for crosstalk and drift using inverse matrix techniques and hysteresis filtering.
key_observables: Mean and maximum residual magnetic fields ($\mu	ext{T}$), Allan deviations ($	ext{nT}$), and spatial variation metrics (RMS variation, volume coverage percentage).
important_parameters: Target residual field $< 1 \mu	ext{T}$; long-duration stability tests (up to $714.4 	ext{ s}$); spatial dimensions ($5 	ext{ mm}$ radius, $10 	imes 5 	imes 5 	ext{ mm}$ ellipsoid).
main_assumptions: The spatial field distribution is reconstructed using a center-constrained quadratic vector model with soft Maxwell regularization, which is an estimation technique.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the closed-loop measurement and control system schematic, the comparison of readout efficiency decay with and without compensation, and spatial slice maps showing reconstructed field anisotropy.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the physical necessity (zero field for quantum memories), then detailing the limitations of existing methods, proposing the integrated hardware/software solution (mechanical, algorithmic, control), and finally presenting extensive experimental validation across temporal stability and spatial mapping.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly detailed engineering blueprint for achieving the necessary ultra-stable magnetic environments required for next-generation quantum memory research, directly impacting the feasibility of quantum information processing using cold atoms.
